thread.title_full: Wall Street Mixed in Early Trading

author: CHAN HO-HIM and ELAINE KURTENBACH - AP Business Writers
title: Wall Street Mixed in Early Trading
text:
• South Korea's Kospi index plunged nearly 11% on heavy selling of computer chipmaking stocks.
• Trading was temporarily halted at times as Kospi dropped to its lowest level since April, closing 10.8% lower at 6,023.66.
• Shares in chipmaker Samsung Electronics sank 13.4% while those of SK Hynix tumbled 14.7%.
• Futures for the S&P 500 were unchanged, while futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.7%.
• Futures for the technology-heavy Nasdaq slid 1% with most chipmakers down anywhere from 2% to 5%.
• SK Hynix's U.S.-traded shares fell to below the $149 initial public offering price for its Wall Street debut earlier this month, closing at $143 a share.
• A 466% jump in the price of Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT in its trading debut Monday underscored concerns about rising competition from Chinese AI startups and chipmakers.
• China has begun mass production of homegrown deep ultraviolet, or DUV, chipmaking tools.
• Shares of Johnson & Johnson rose 3% after the drugmaker agreed to pay $5.5 billion to settle remaining lawsuits that claim its talc products caused ovarian cancer.
• Coca-Cola Co. jumped 4.5% after it beat Wall Street's sales and profit targets.
• United Parcel Service reported strong earnings for its most recent quarter but its shares rose a modest 1%.
• Tokyo's Nikkei 225 dropped 4% to 62,364.92.
• The Taiex in Taiwan skidded 4.7%, with shares of leading chipmaker TSMC falling 3%.
• Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained 0.4% to 25,310.85.
• The Shanghai Composite index lost 1.2% to 3,813.31.
• Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.6% to 8,947.80.
• India's Sensex edged 0.1% lower.
• Germany's DAX and the CAC 40 in Paris were each up less than 0.1%, while Britain's FTSE 100 picked up 0.5%.
• Oil prices extended their declines as the U.S. and Iran refrained from strikes in their on-again, off-again war.
• Brent crude fell $1.35 to $84.52 a barrel.
• U.S. benchmark crude oil lost 81 cents to $81.80 a barrel.
summary: Wall Street is mixed in early trading Tuesday with chipmakers getting hit again after a huge sell-off in South Korea. South Korea’s Kospi index plunged nearly 11% Tuesday on heavy selling of computer chipmaking stocks that have been battered recently by fears that the AI boom may turn out to be a bubble. Tuesday’s chip stock sell-off also followed a report in the technology news publication The Information that China has begun mass production of homegrown deep ultraviolet, or DUV, chipmaking tools.
